text:
tara: Security advisory 3: Weve flagged a batch of company Mac laptops that are NOT encrypted or are running unsupported macOS builds with a publicly disclosed kernel vuln (CVE-2026-2147). Affected inventory: 18 devices across eng and data teams. This is a required remediation. Deadline: 72 hours from this post.

mac-admin: TL;DR - If your Mac shows FileVault: Off or is on macOS < 13.6.1, follow remediation steps below. We will escalate any noncompliant device to People Ops and may enforce a remote lock/wipe for devices out of compliance after the deadline.

jordan: How did we detect this?

tara: We ran an MDM compliance sweep and cross-checked disk-encryption state with our vulnerability scanner. The kernel vuln is actively weaponized in the wild for local privilege escalation; combined with unencrypted disks this raises a serious exfil risk.

mac-admin: Quick local checks you can run now:

```bash
# FileVault status
sudo fdesetup status

# macOS version
sw_vers -productVersion

# check for kernel vuln indicators (MDM telemetry will verify)
/usr/sbin/system_profiler SPSoftwareDataType | grep -i 'System Version' -A1
```

mac-admin: Remediation steps (required):
1) Enable FileVault immediately (follow company MDM flow if enrolled). If youre not enrolled, enroll first.
2) Update macOS to the minimum supported patch: macOS 13.6.1+ (or the latest available patch for your machine).
3) Ensure FileVault recovery key is escrowed to our MDM (do not store keys in personal notes).
4) Confirm compliance by uploading the output of `sudo fdesetup status` and `sw_vers -productVersion` to ticket SEC-3409.

mac-admin: FileVault enable example (if not managed):
```bash
# start enable, follow the UI to set a password and escrow the key
sudo fdesetup enable -usertoadd $(whoami)
```

people-ops: If you have a corporate-lent device and cannot complete this within 72h due to travel or lack of network, DM People Ops ASAP. We will provision a temporary replacement or help schedule a secure update window.

jordan: What about Homebrew or custom kernels? Will that break FileVault or update flows?

mac-admin: Usually not. If you have kernel extensions (kexts) or Brew-installed kernel-level tooling, contact us via DM before updating so we can advise. Well whitelist or provide a staged patching path.

sec-ops: Automated enforcement plan: 1) Org-wide verification scan in 24h 2) Reminder DM to flagged owners in 48h 3) If still noncompliant at 72h, escalate to manager + People Ops and schedule device lock/wipe for corporate-devices. Non-corporate BYOD will be removed from corporate network access until remediated.

sec-bot: Created ticket SEC-3409 and kicked off initial MDM compliance query. Scheduled auto-reminder: 2026-03-28T15:00:00Z. This is a required company security action.

tara: If youre unsure whether your device is company-managed: run `profiles status -type enrollment` and DM mac-admin.

mac-admin: Links: Enrollment guide: https://redwood.internal/docs/mac/mdm-enroll, macOS update steps: https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT204204

jordan: Done 3 - SEC-3409-7 (uploaded fdesetup output).

mac-admin: Thanks. Marked as compliant.

people-ops: Reminder: any device that requires a wipe will have a manager notification and a 24h grace window before action.

sec-ops: Appreciate the quick fixes. If you hit blockers (firmware password, corporate encryption policies), ping @mac-admin or open an urgent ticket in SEC-3409 with "FW: blocker".

tara: Closing note: sharing a short script to gather diagnostics if you want to paste into SEC-3409 quickly:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
echo "host: $(hostname)"
echo "user: $(whoami)"

echo "fdesetup:"
sudo fdesetup status || true

echo "version:"
sw_vers -productVersion

echo "profiles:"
profiles status -type enrollment || true
```

sec-bot: Final reminder will post 12h before deadline. Comply ASAP. @here
